tsa.note: Larger liquids go in checked bags. Medicines, baby formula, breast milk and baby food over 3.4 oz are allowed in carry-on and need not fit in the bag.

uk.bag: one clear resealable bag of about 1 litre (about 20 × 20 cm), unless the airport says otherwise
uk.bigBag: no plastic bag needed, liquids stay in your bag
uk.note100: This airport keeps the 100 ml limit per container. Medicines, special-diet food and baby milk up to 2 litres are allowed at every UK airport.
uk.noteLarge: This airport’s own page states the larger limit. Your return airport may still apply 100 ml.

batteries.noteUs: FAA PackSafe: spare lithium batteries and power banks travel in the cabin only.
batteries.noteUk: CAA: at most two power banks per person, never recharged on board.

powerBankAirlines.useOnboard: allowed to charge devices except during taxi, take-off and landing; power banks may not be recharged onboard
powerBankAirlines.quote: Power banks are limited to a maximum of 2 per passenger [...] Power banks cannot be recharged at any time when onboard/ during the flight (e.g., one power bank charging another). Power banks may be used to charge personal electronic devices, except during taxi, take-off, and landing, or when instructed otherwise by the crew. Power banks and spare lithium batteries cannot be placed in cabin baggage stored in the overhead lockers. [...] Devices or batteries over 100Wh are not permitted, neither in the cabin nor the hold (with the exception of Electric Wheelchair batteries).

powerBankAirlines.useOnboard: prohibited (must not be used to charge other devices)
powerBankAirlines.quote: Power banks are accepted on easyJet aircraft with a Wh rating not exceeding 160Wh for lithium batteries. Power banks are prohibited from use on easyJet aircraft and must not be used to charge other devices. [...] Maximum of two power banks permitted per customer. Power banks must be carried in carry-on baggage only

powerBankAirlines.useOnboard: must not be charged onboard and should not be used in-flight (same page also says not to charge devices during taxi, take-off and landing)
powerBankAirlines.quote: Customers may carry no more than 2 power banks per person, not exceeding 160Wh, providing they are individually protected against short circuit. In all cases: these must not be charged whilst onboard the aircraft, and should not be used in-flight.

powerBankAirlines.useOnboard: seat power may not be used to charge power banks; power banks stored in seat pocket or under-seat bag (no explicit ban on using them to charge devices)
powerBankAirlines.quote: Power bank limits: Up to 2 power banks per person Power banks must display capacity rating information. Aircraft seat power supplies are to be used exclusively for charging personal electronic devices (PEDs), not power banks. Power banks must be stored either in the seat pocket or in a bag placed under the seat in front. Power banks must not exceed 100Wh

Power banks are not to be used during any phase of the flight duration! [...] Each person is limited to a maximum of 20 spare batteries, including maximum 1 power bank. Power banks exceeding 100 Wh are forbidden.
